related_questions.question: Has anyone survived stage 4 breast cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, people can and do survive stage 4 breast cancer, though it's not considered curable in most cases. While the five-year survival rate for stage 4 breast cancer is around 32%, meaning that 32% of women with this diagnosis are still alive five years later, many individuals live much longer, even beyond 10 years, thanks to advancements in treatment and personalized approaches. Some individuals with stage 4 breast cancer achieve long-term remission, where their cancer is controlled and undetectable, though they still require ongoing treatment and monitoring.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, people can and do survive stage 4 breast cancer, though it's not considered curable in most cases

list.title: Not Curable, But Treatable:
list.snippet: Stage 4 breast cancer, also known as metastatic breast cancer, means the cancer has spread to other parts of the body beyond the breast and nearby lymph nodes. While it's not curable in most cases, it is treatable, and treatments can help control the disease, improve quality of life, and extend survival.

list.title: Five-Year Survival Rates:
list.snippet: The five-year survival rate for stage 4 breast cancer is around 32%, meaning that 32% of women diagnosed with stage 4 breast cancer are still alive five years later. This number can vary based on factors like the specific subtype of breast cancer, the extent of metastasis, and the individual's overall health.

list.title: Long-Term Survival:
list.snippet: While the median survival time for stage 4 breast cancer is around three years, many individuals live much longer, with some surviving 10 years or more. A study from 2016 showed that about 13% of women with primary stage 4 breast cancer survive for 10 years or more.

list.title: Remission:
list.snippet: Some individuals with stage 4 breast cancer can achieve remission, where their cancer is undetectable and under control, though this often requires ongoing treatment and monitoring, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

list.title: Factors Influencing Survival:
list.snippet: Several factors can influence survival, including the specific subtype of breast cancer (e.g., HER2-positive, triple-negative), the extent of metastasis, the individual's overall health, and their response to treatment.

list.title: Personalized Treatment:
list.snippet: Advances in treatment, such as targeted therapies and immunotherapies, along with a more personalized approach to treatment, have contributed to improved outcomes for some individuals with stage 4 breast cancer, according to the Rogel Cancer Center.

list.title: Inspiration from Survivors:
list.snippet: Many individuals with stage 4 breast cancer have lived for many years after their diagnosis, sharing their stories and inspiring others to live with hope and determination.

Tumor type: Triple-negative breast cancer has a lower survival rate than other types.
